summary.text: Mammals are vertebrate animals marked by milk-producing mammary glands, fur or hair, a broad neocortex and three middle ear bones.
Their ancestors diverged from those of reptiles and birds over 300 million years ago, and mammals have been the dominant land animals since 66 million years ago.
Around 6,640 living species are described in 27 orders, ranging from the 30 to 40 millimetre bumblebee bat to the 30 metre blue whale.

items.prompt: A zookeeper needs one finding that would settle whether an unfamiliar animal is a mammal. Which would do it?

options.label: It lays eggs in a nest it builds
It lives in the water all its life
It has glands that make milk to feed its young
It can move through the air on wings

items.explain: Milk-producing mammary glands are a defining mammal trait. Egg-laying, life at sea and flight all occur among mammals or other animals, so none of them settles it.

items.prompt: A visitor is puzzled that the platypus lays eggs yet is called a mammal. What resolves this?

options.label: It belongs to the five monotreme species, the only modern mammals that lay eggs
Its eggs hatch inside its body, so it still gives live birth
Mammals living near water are allowed to lay eggs
It is classified as a reptile despite being called a mammal

items.explain: All modern mammals give birth to live young except the five monotreme species, which lay eggs; platypuses are monotremes.

items.prompt: A student claims mammals reached their modern variety while non-avian dinosaurs still thrived. What is the correction?

options.label: That variety came earlier, in the Carboniferous alongside the first reptiles
That variety arrived with the first farming societies
That variety came once birds had evolved from mammals
That variety came later, after non-avian dinosaurs had gone extinct

items.explain: Mammals achieved their modern diversity in the Paleogene and Neogene, after the extinction of non-avian dinosaurs.

items.prompt: A biologist finds small bones deep inside a whale's body where hind legs would sit on a land animal. What do they show?

options.label: Young limbs that will grow out in adulthood
Leftover rear limbs from the four-limbed mammal body type
A third set of ear bones used for hearing
Evidence that the animal is not a mammal at all

items.explain: The basic mammal body type has four limbs, and in cetaceans the rear limbs are mere internal vestiges.

items.prompt: A band of nomads begins keeping herds of tamed animals year after year. What larger change did this practice help drive?

options.label: Societies broke into smaller and more isolated wandering bands
Food came mainly from farming rather than hunting and gathering
Hunting became the main source of food everywhere
The tamed animals lost their fur and mammary glands

items.explain: Domestication played a major role in the Neolithic Revolution, when farming replaced hunting and gathering and societies shifted from nomadic to settled.

items.prompt: A student asks which official classification of mammals every scientist must use. What is the accurate reply?

options.label: None is universally accepted, though Simpson's system is the closest to official
Linnaeus's original system, which has never been revised
Wilson and Reeder's 2005 system, which replaced all others
The IUCN's 2008 assessment, which settled the debate

items.explain: Classification has been revised several times and no system is universally accepted; Simpson's remains the closest thing to an official one despite known issues.
